rationale: All three lenses ran; the ticket's five acceptance criteria pass and the fix is sound, but one security-guide violation (CR-001: a JSON.parse error message that can quote part of a secret-bearing CODEMIE_PROFILE_CONFIG is written to the debug log) and one plan-required test assertion that is missing (CR-002) must be fixed. The ticket text was supplied inline as the acceptance source (sdlc-light has no spec.md). Dismissed ~14 lens concerns (CODEMIE_PROFILE_CONFIG/CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR env trust is the existing codebase trust model, launch-snapshot precedence is intended, partial launcher-config shapes are unreachable because the launcher always writes provider and baseUrl, stale inherited env travels with the matching proxy env). Deferred 3 pre-existing/out-of-scope items: Copilot hook payload cwd vs process.cwd(), the malformed-launch-config fallback reading a loopback CODEMIE_BASE_URL via ConfigLoader, and walk-up helper coupling to identity-fields.

business_review.item: AC1: SSO validation uses the same profile as the active Claude Code session
business_review.notes: resolveHookAuthProfile() prefers the launch profile in CODEMIE_PROFILE_CONFIG (exported at AgentCLI.ts:418); claude-code-otlp ensureProxyAuth now uses it; plugin test asserts the gate receives the session profile even when ConfigLoader.load would return Preview.
CODEMIE_PROFILE_CONFIG is the resolved launch config with --profile already applied and wins over any config lookup; covered by the 'regardless of cwd' helper test.

business_review.item: AC3: Moving between repository subdirectories does not change the authentication environment
business_review.notes: Env path ignores cwd; no-env fallback walks up from CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR or cwd to the nearest local .codemie; covered by nested-cwd and CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR tests.

business_review.item: AC4: Production sessions never open Preview SSO unexpectedly
business_review.notes: Ticket repro (Production env profile, no local config in cwd, global Preview active) yields Production gate input in the helper test; same fix applied to copilot-cli-otlp and copilot-chat-otlp.

business_review.item: AC5: Regression tests cover nested directories and different local/global profiles
business_review.notes: hook-auth-profile.test.ts uses the real ConfigLoader with a global Preview profile and a repo-local Production profile; each plugin test adds a session-profile case.

business_review.item: Fail-closed preserved: a ConfigLoader.load failure in the fallback propagates to the plugin catch
business_review.notes: Helper does not catch; 'propagates ConfigLoader.load failures' test; Copilot 'disk full' tests now reject via the helper.

business_review.item: CODEMIE_BASE_URL never read on the launch path; ssoUrl stays codeMieUrl || baseUrl; gate contract unchanged
business_review.notes: Gate signatures and call shapes are unchanged; ssoUrl derivation matches in both paths.

business_review.item: One shared helper used by all three ensureProxyAuth() copies; ConfigLoader untouched
business_review.notes: All three plugins wired; unused ConfigLoader imports dropped; identity-fields.ts only gains an export.

business_review.item: Plan test detail: plugin regression tests also assert ConfigLoader.load was not called
business_review.notes: The three plugin tests assert the gate argument but never assert the ConfigLoader.load decoy was left unused, so the decoy is vestigial (raised as CR-002).

standards_review.notes: Three commits use type fix, allowed scope agents, subjects under 100 chars, ticket key present.
ESM with .js imports, interface for shapes, explicit return types on exports, no any, lint and typecheck clean.
No attribution headers touched; but the debug log of a raw JSON.parse error message for CODEMIE_PROFILE_CONFIG may echo part of a secret-bearing config (AGENTS.md: never log raw secrets; see CR-001).

findings.title: Debug log may echo secret-bearing config text
findings.problem: readLaunchProfile logs `error.message` of a failed JSON.parse of CODEMIE_PROFILE_CONFIG. V8 JSON.parse messages quote a snippet of the input, and this variable holds the whole resolved launch config, which can include apiKey or JWT values.
findings.impact: A malformed/truncated CODEMIE_PROFILE_CONFIG with debug logging enabled can write part of a credential to the log, contrary to the repo rule to never log raw secrets.
findings.recommendation: Log a fixed string (e.g. 'ignoring malformed CODEMIE_PROFILE_CONFIG') without the parse error text. Also reword the doc comment so it says the launch path never reads CODEMIE_BASE_URL (the ConfigLoader fallback still honours CODEMIE_* env).

findings.title: Plugin tests leave the ConfigLoader decoy unasserted
findings.problem: The session-profile test in each of the three plugin test files (claude-code-otlp, copilot-cli-otlp, copilot-chat-otlp) plants a Preview ConfigLoader.load decoy but never asserts it stayed unused, and never pins that the plugin calls resolveHookAuthProfile() with no arguments; the plan required the not-called assertion.
findings.impact: The decoy is vestigial and the tests only prove pass-through of a mocked value, so a regression that reads the cwd config alongside the helper, or passes an argument that bypasses launch env, would go unnoticed.
findings.recommendation: In each of the three tests add `expect(resolveHookAuthProfile).toHaveBeenCalledWith()` and, where the plugin has no other ConfigLoader.load caller on that path, `expect(ConfigLoader.load).not.toHaveBeenCalled()`; if a remaining caller makes the not-called assertion unreliable, drop the decoy instead and say why.
